definition: Infectious disease caused by the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2).
transmission_causes: Breathing in respiratory droplets from an infected person
Close contact (touching, shaking hands) with an infected person and then touching the face
Touching a contaminated surface and then touching the face
general_prevention: Getting vaccinated against COVID-19 and the flu
Washing hands frequently with soap and water (or using hand sanitizer)
Wearing a multilayer, snug-fitting mask (like N95 or KN95) in indoor public spaces or around others
Avoiding close contact and sharing items with sick or exposed people
Maintaining distance / limiting exposure to large indoor gatherings or high-risk events
Quitting smoking and avoiding secondhand smoke
Getting treated for underlying health conditions that increase risk

manifestations_and_subtypes.definition: SARS-CoV-2 infection occurring in pediatric populations (infants, children, and adolescents).
diagnosis: Laboratory test (saliva sample or swab from nose or throat)
treatments: Staying hydrated with plenty of fluids
Care at a hospital or ICU
outlook: Most kids get better within one to two weeks
Children who develop complications may need longer to recover
Most kids recover and bounce back just fine
Some children develop post-COVID conditions (long COVID)
living_with: Follow healthcare provider's and school/daycare's advice about returning to school
Tell pediatrician if child has lingering or new symptoms

manifestations_and_subtypes.definition: SARS-CoV-2 infection occurring during pregnancy, posing unique risks to both maternal and fetal health.
symptoms: Severe fever (higher than 103 degrees Fahrenheit or 39 degrees Celsius)
Lethargy or having trouble staying awake
New loss of taste or smell
Pain or pressure in your chest
Disorientation or confusion / inability to wake up
diagnosis: Diagnosis based on symptoms and likelihood of exposure
Laboratory test involving swabbing nasal fluid
treatments: Using a humidifier to relieve congestion
Taking over-the-counter medication containing dextromethorphan to reduce coughing
Treatment in a hospital for severe symptoms
complications: Heavy bleeding right after giving birth (postpartum hemorrhage)
Inflammatory responses in the developing fetus
Vertical transmission (spreading of virus from pregnant woman to fetus)
outlook: Most pregnant women who get COVID-19 experience mild symptoms and fully recover
Birth defects due to COVID-19 are rare
living_with: Rest plenty and drink a lot of water
Isolate from others living with you until feeling better
Communicate with healthcare provider and follow their advice

manifestations_and_subtypes.definition: A severe lung complication of COVID-19 where the virus causes inflammation and fluid leakage into the alveoli.
causes: Infection with the SARS-CoV-2 virus in your lungs
Immune system attacking the infection causing alveoli to swell and leak fluid
symptoms: Shortness of breath or trouble breathing
diagnosis: Asking about symptoms and physical examination
treatments: Draining of fluids with a catheter or surgery
outlook: Can last longer and cause damage in more places than other types of pneumonia
Probably need to stay in the hospital for a week or longer to recover
How soon you feel better depends on age, severity of pneumonia, and other health conditions or complications
Might still be more tired than usual or have other symptoms for weeks or months after going home
Mortality rates range from 3% to 5% for hospital patients not in ICU, 30% to 40% for people in the ICU, and 50% to 80% for those on a respirator
Age is usually the biggest factor in surviving COVID pneumonia
living_with: Follow up with your healthcare provider if you have ongoing health concerns after being treated

manifestations_and_subtypes.definition: A post-acute sequela characterized by persistent, returning, or new health problems occurring weeks or months after an initial SARS-CoV-2 infection.
causes: Viral persistence (SARS‑CoV‑2 hanging around in the body)
Reactivation of other viruses (such as Epstein-Barr virus)
Long-term psychological effects of having a serious illness
symptoms: Loss of or altered sense of smell or taste (anosmia or dysgeusia)
diagnosis: Listening to symptoms and health history
treatments: Medication (for cough, headaches, anxiety, depression, or underlying causes like blood clots)
prevention: Antiviral medications (nirmatrelvir / Paxlovid® within five days of a positive COVID test or symptom start)
outlook: Symptoms may come and go, change or get worse over time
Many long-haulers do eventually get better, though how long that takes is different for each person
Most people with long COVID start to feel better within 12 to 18 months
living_with: See a primary care provider (PCP) and one or more specialists or a long COVID clinic
Be persistent and patient while trying treatments
Allow yourself more time for normal tasks and take more breaks
Take extended time off work or school if needed
